 Follow Us On: News Education Today CISCE board exam datesheet 2027 out: ICSE Class 10 begins Feb 15, ISC from Feb 9 CISCE board exam datesheet 2027 out: ICSE Class 10 begins Feb 15, ISC from Feb 9
 The Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE) has released the ICSE and ISC examination timetables for students appearing for the Class 10 and Class 12 board exams. The schedules include subject-wise exam dates and timings, helping students plan their revision and preparation.
 Advertisement ICSE, ISC datesheet 2027 out at cisce.org: Direct link to check CISCE Class 10, 12 timetables(Photo: PTI) By: India Today Education Desk New Delhi , Nov 10, 2026 15:20 IST Last Updated Nov 10, 2026 15:20 IST Published by Devika Bhattacharya Nov 10, 2026 14:48 IST The Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE) has released the examination timetable for the ICSE (Class 10) and ISC (Class 12) board examinations 2027. Students appearing for the examinations can check and download the subject-wise datesheet from the council's official website, cisce.org.
 According to the schedule, the ICSE Class 10 examinations will begin on February 15 and conclude on March 31, 2027. The examinations will be conducted across 2,835 centres in India and overseas.
 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Meanwhile, the ISC Class 12 examinations will commence on February 9 and conclude on April 8, 2027.
 CISCE will conduct the two examinations for a combined total of 3,79,980 candidates. Of these, 2,69,955 students from 3,106 affiliated schools will appear for the ICSE examination, while 1,10,025 candidates from 1,651 schools will take the ISC examination.
 The ICSE examination will cover 76 subjects, while the ISC examination will include 60 subjects. STATE-WISE CANDIDATE DISTRIBUTION
 Uttar Pradesh has recorded the highest number of ICSE candidates, with 51,168 students. It is followed by West Bengal with 46,521 candidates, Karnataka with 33,417, Maharashtra with 31,035, Punjab with 19,308 and Jharkhand with 17,201.
 For the ISC Year 2027 examination, Uttar Pradesh again accounts for the highest number of candidates, with 34,702 students. West Bengal follows with 30,235 candidates.
 Other states with a significant number of ISC candidates include Uttarakhand (5,629), Punjab (5,479), Jharkhand (5,356), Maharashtra (4,660), Tamil Nadu (3,572), Kerala (3,491) and Karnataka (3,010).
 The ISC examination will be held across 1,477 centres in India and overseas. ICSE BOARD EXAM 2026 TIMETABLE

 ICSE BOARD EXAM 2027: REVISED TIMINGS
 A major change in the ICSE 2027 examination schedule is the revised exam timings. The reading time for question papers will begin at 10 am, while the writing time will commence at 10:15 am. In the previous schedule, reading time was set for 10:45 am, followed by the examination at 11 am.
 advertisement Candidates appearing for the ICSE 2027 examinations must report to their respective examination halls or rooms and be seated by 9:45 am. CISCE STRESSES FAIR EXAMS
 CISCE has reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring credibility, fairness and transparency in its examinations. The ICSE and ISC examinations will be conducted across 2,835 and 1,477 centres, respectively, in India and overseas.
 Dr Joseph Emmanuel, Chief Executive and Secretary of CISCE, said that a credible examination system depends on fair processes, transparent administration and the trust of students, parents and institutions.
 He added that the council would continue to uphold these principles through robust examination protocols, transparent procedures and consistent assessment standards, ensuring equal opportunities for all candidates to demonstrate their learning. CISCE STRENGTHENS COMPETENCY-BASED ASSESSMENT
 In line with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, CISCE is strengthening its assessment framework to focus on conceptual understanding, practical application, critical thinking and problem-solving skills.
 Dr Joseph Emmanuel said the council's focus on competency-based assessments is intended to encourage students to apply their knowledge, think critically and find solutions to real-world problems. He added that the approach aligns with NEP 2020 and the changing expectations of higher education and industry, helping students prepare for challenges beyond examinations.
 advertisement Further, CISCE will begin distributing admission cards for the ICSE and ISC Year 2027 examinations in mid-December 2026. - Ends
